text: The additive map inserts x at its specified index and zero elsewhere, the summand inclusion of [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). Its support lies in that singleton, and evaluation at the index recovers x. The same construction works for additive commutative monoids and dependent component types. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L129).

Evaluating the included element at its own index returns x. This is the defining coordinate of the summand inclusion in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22), and the pinned value is DFinsupp.single. It holds for zero as well as nonzero x and needs no cancellation hypothesis. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L135).

An element inserted at i has zero at every different index j, precisely the single-support inclusion in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). The explicit hypothesis j≠i is correctly oriented for the evaluated coordinate. This statement makes no restriction on the other component modules. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L138).

Every finitely supported family is a finite sum of its single-coordinate insertions. A predicate containing zero and these generators and closed under addition therefore holds on every family. This is induction on the direct-sum representation in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22), including zero and an empty index type. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L181).

At coordinate j, only the insertion indexed by j can contribute, and outside the support xⱼ is already zero. Thus the displayed finite sum reconstructs x, as in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22)’s direct-sum description. The decidability hypotheses expose the actual finite support; no infinite summation occurs. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L165).

The map sums φᵢ(xᵢ) over the finite support. Additivity and zero preservation make the result independent of padding by zeros, and restriction to a summand recovers φᵢ. This is the additive-monoid version of the coproduct map in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22); commutative addition makes ordering immaterial. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L221).

The universal map evaluated on a single-coordinate insertion leaves exactly φᵢ(x), because all other inputs are zero and each φ preserves zero. This is the defining commutative triangle of [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22), generalized to additive commutative monoids. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L225).

Canonical summation sends an element inserted from Aᵢ to its underlying element of M. This is [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22)’s coproduct computation applied to the subtype inclusions. The equation is valid even when summands overlap; it asserts this evaluation and does not require summation to be injective. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L421).

After forgetting membership proofs, the j-coordinate is x when i=j and zero otherwise. Both branches are compared in the common ambient M, so dependent component types cause no mismatch. This is the coordinate formula for the inclusions in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean#L426).

Injectivity of canonical recomposition prevents a nonzero element of one piece from also lying in the sum of the others, giving lattice independence. This is the independence part of the direct decomposition in [Hazrat §1.2.1](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21). This direction works for semirings; the converse requires additional hypotheses. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L457).

Surjectivity of canonical summation writes every element of M as a finite sum from the pieces. Since the range of that map is their supremum, the supremum equals top. This is the spanning part of [Hazrat §1.2.1](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/LAG/man/514.pdf#page=21)’s internal direct decomposition, with no finiteness assumption on the index family. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L452).

The spanning hypothesis gives surjectivity of canonical summation. Over a ring, [Mathlib’s independence criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/DFinsupp.lean#L581) gives uniqueness of finite expressions, hence injectivity. Together these are IsInternal. The displayed Ring and AddCommGroup assumptions retain the subtraction needed for this independence argument. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L510).

Decompose into summands, express each component in its given basis, then flatten the finite supports. This gives the coordinate equivalence required by [Mathlib’s basis representation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean#L19), with basis indices (i,a) recording their summand. No basis is chosen anew, and neither index family must be finite. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L462).

The collected basis vector at (i,a) is exactly the underlying vector vᵢ(a) in M. Reversing the construction sends the single coordinate at (i,a) through the i-th basis and the summand inclusion, as prescribed by [Mathlib’s basis representation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean#L19). The dependent pair retains both indices. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L471).

The collected vector at (i,a) equals the underlying element vᵢ(a), which belongs to Aᵢ by its subtype. This gives the stated membership directly from [Mathlib’s basis representation](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Basis/Defs.lean#L19)’s coordinate construction. It assigns membership in the indexed piece without claiming a unique degree for every vector. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L476).

Agreement after every summand inclusion determines agreement on each finite sum of included elements, hence on the whole direct sum. This is uniqueness in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). The hypotheses compare maps on entire summands, with no basis or finite-generation assumption. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L136).

With a finite index type, every family automatically has finite support. Forgetting the support and equipping a family with this finite support are inverse linear maps. Thus direct sum and product coincide in this case, by the finite-support definition preceding [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L150).

Apply each supplied linear equivalence to its own coordinate; the inverse applies the component inverses. Both preserve zero and finite support, and their composites are coordinatewise identities. This is the componentwise isomorphism induced by the direct-sum universal property in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L587).

The map sends a family indexed by (i,j) to its rows indexed first by i and then by j. Finite total support gives finitely many nonzero rows, while finitely many finite row supports flatten to finite support. The coordinatewise inverse is linear, matching [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22)’s finite-support construction. See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L372).

Reindexing along h sends the coordinate at h⁻¹(k) to coordinate k, so the target family is correctly M(h.symm k). The inverse uses h and both preserve finite support and scalar operations. This realizes relabeling of the direct sum defined in [Conrad, Theorem 7.4](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/universalmapping.pdf#page=22). See the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean#L321).

Precomposition with H→H/I gives the group inclusion Hom(H/I,A)→Hom(H,A), matching [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). Published [injectivity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L104) and [naturality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Naturality.lean#L41) controls pass. Points are algebra maps with convolution, for every commutative value algebra A; this is the subgroup represented by H/I, not a quotient of the ambient point group.
Quotient-point inclusion is injective for every value algebra.
Quotient-point inclusion is natural in the value algebra.

The included point is the composite f∘q with q:H→H/I, consistent with [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [elementwise evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L82) control passes. WithConv changes the group operation to convolution while retaining the same underlying algebra map; the arrow reverses the coordinate quotient direction.
Included quotient point evaluates as f([h]).

Evaluation at h is f([h]), the pointwise quotient-composition formula underlying [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [lift-recovery control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L133) passes. Both sides are elements of A, and the ideal used in [h] is I.toIdeal; the formula applies to every h without selecting a quotient representative.
Factoring then including a vanishing point recovers the original point.

Two algebra maps out of H/I agreeing after its surjective projection agree on every quotient class, the uniqueness in [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [universal-quotient-point control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L74) passes. Injectivity holds for each value algebra A; no field, reducedness, or density of rational points is needed.
Universal quotient points recover ideal inclusion from all-value-algebra subgroup inclusions.

The assumption g(I)=0 makes [h]↦g(h) a well-defined algebra map H/I→A, exactly [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). Published [class evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L121) and [recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L133) controls pass. The value algebra A needs no Hopf structure: this constructs a point, not a Hopf-algebra morphism to A.
Factored point evaluates on [h] as g(h).
Factoring then including a vanishing point recovers the original point.

The factor point takes [h] to g(h), the defining evaluation law of [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). Vanishing on I makes the value independent of the representative. The published [recovery control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L133) passes; the docstring’s representative language does not introduce a chosen section of H→H/I.
Factoring then including a vanishing point recovers the original point.

Factoring g through H/I and precomposing with q recovers g on every h, the factorization identity in [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [image characterization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L162) control passes. The vanishing assumption is explicit; the theorem does not factor arbitrary ambient points through a prescribed quotient.
The range of quotient points is precisely the points vanishing on I.

The quotient-point inclusion is a group homomorphism, so it preserves the commutator of the two lifted points; evaluation then gives the displayed equality, consistent with [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). Published [evaluation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L82) and [recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L133) controls pass. The bracket is the group commutator for convolution, not a Lie bracket or subtraction of maps.
Included quotient point evaluates as f([h]).
Factoring then including a vanishing point recovers the original point.

An ambient algebra map factors through H/I exactly when it kills I, precisely [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). Published [zero-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) and [augmentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L212) controls pass. This describes the image on A-points for each A, without replacing I by its radical or restricting to ground-field points.
The zero ideal cuts out all ambient points.
Augmentation ideal cuts out exactly the identity point.

Taking the range of the quotient-point homomorphism gives the subgroup represented by H/I, matching [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). Published [vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L193) and [zero-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) controls pass. The elements are algebra maps into A with convolution; neither all ambient points nor an abstract quotient point group is substituted.
Cut-out subgroup membership is precisely vanishing on the ideal.
The zero ideal cuts out all ambient points.

Membership means the algebra map annihilates I, by the factorization property of [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [all-value-algebras control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L74) passes and recovers the original ideal order using a universal quotient point. The criterion does not identify ideals merely from points over one field, which could miss infinitesimal structure.
Universal quotient points recover ideal inclusion from all-value-algebra subgroup inclusions.

Killing ker ε forces g(x)=algebraMap(ε(x)), since x−algebraMap(ε(x)) lies in the augmentation ideal. This is the identity point in [Milne, Proposition 3.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=79). The published [augmentation equivalence](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L212) control passes. The conclusion is the convolution identity, not the zero map, over every commutative value algebra.
Augmentation ideal cuts out exactly the identity point.

Vanishing on J.map φ is equivalent to vanishing on the generators φ(J), hence to (f∘φ)(J)=0, by [Mathlib’s ideal image](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L43). The published [vanishing control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L193) passes. Ideal.map is the generated ideal, so the equivalence needs no surjectivity of φ and does not confuse ideal image with set image.
Cut-out subgroup membership is precisely vanishing on the ideal.

Surjectivity lets every y∈I be lifted to x∈f⁻¹(I), so g∘f kills f⁻¹(I) exactly when g kills I, using [Mathlib’s ideal image](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L43). Published [surjective order-reflection](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L132) and [vanishing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L193) controls pass. The explicit surjectivity hypothesis is essential for the forward implication.
Surjective ideal pullback reflects and preserves containment.
Cut-out subgroup membership is precisely vanishing on the ideal.

The included quotient point belongs to the range defining the cut-out subgroup, with itself as witness; this realizes [Mathlib’s algebra quotient lift](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean#L482). The published [universal quotient control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L74) passes using this membership for the identity point of H/J. No arbitrary ambient point is asserted to lift.
Universal quotient points recover ideal inclusion from all-value-algebra subgroup inclusions.

A point killing J also kills I whenever I≤J, giving the reversed subgroup inclusion described by [Milne, Proposition 1.49](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [zero-ideal](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) and [order-recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L74) controls pass. Antitone refers to ideals versus subgroup inclusion; it does not claim that one value algebra detects all strict containments.
The zero ideal cuts out all ambient points.
Universal quotient points recover ideal inclusion from all-value-algebra subgroup inclusions.

The larger ideal imposes more vanishing equations, so its A-point subgroup lies inside the smaller ideal’s subgroup, as in [Milne, Proposition 1.49](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [naturality-of-inclusion control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L145) passes. The direction agrees with H/I→H/J on coordinates and reverses on represented points.
Ideal-induced subgroup inclusions commute with value-algebra maps.

If g vanishes on J and I≤J, it vanishes on I, the membership form of the subgroup order in [Milne, Proposition 1.49](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). The published [join/intersection control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L128) passes. Both memberships use the same ambient Hopf algebra and value algebra, so no point transport or additional field hypothesis is hidden.
Join of ideals cuts out intersection of point subgroups.

Vanishing on I⊔J is equivalent to vanishing on both ideals: each element of the sum is y+z and algebra maps are additive. This matches [Milne, Proposition 1.49](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=31). Published [zero-ideal boundary](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L114) and [containment](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Order.lean#L67) controls pass. The right-hand meet is intersection of point subgroups, including over nonreduced A.
The zero ideal cuts out all ambient points.
Larger ideal yields a smaller A-point subgroup.

Pullback along e and e⁻¹ gives inverse order maps on Hopf ideals; quotient isomorphisms preserve P. Thus every smaller P-ideal pulls back to one below I and equals it by [Mathlib’s minimality criterion](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Order/Minimal.lean#L252). The published [maximal-torus transport control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Torus/Maximal.lean#L88) passes. Minimal is not least: no uniqueness, existence or monotonicity of P is assumed.
Maximal-torus status transports in both directions under an ambient isomorphism.
Pullback along an equivalence then its inverse recovers the ideal.

For finite positive p, membership means summability of the pth powers of coordinate norms. At infinity it means bounded coordinates; at zero it explicitly means finite support. This matches classical sequence spaces in the usual range and states its endpoint convention without claiming a norm for every p. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/measure_theory/measure_notes.pdf#page=83) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L77).

The carrier is the additive subgroup of families satisfying Memℓp. Closure under addition is proved separately for finite support, boundedness and positive powers, including 0<p<1. No norm topology is inherited from the product: the PreLp type synonym leaves that choice to the later normed-group instance. Compared with [the reference](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/01/09/245b-notes-3-lp-spaces/) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L369).

A bounded family of coordinate norms belongs to ℓ∞. This is the intended bounded-sequence condition, generalized to arbitrary dependent index families; it does not require decay, continuity of the indexing map or attainment of the bound. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L92).

The assigned size is support cardinality at p=0, the supremum norm at infinity, and the pth-root sum for finite positive p. A Norm instance only supplies this real-valued function. It does not assert the triangle inequality or scalar homogeneity at exponents where those fail. Compared with [the reference](https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~hunter/measure_theory/measure_notes.pdf#page=83) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L440).

For 1≤p≤∞ the specified ℓp size gives a normed additive group. The finite-p triangle inequality uses Minkowski; the infinity branch uses coordinate bounds. Separation follows from the coordinate norms. The explicit p≥1 premise avoids asserting a triangle inequality for the usual p-size below one. Compared with [the reference](https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2009/01/09/245b-notes-3-lp-spaces/) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Lp/lpSpace.lean#L545).

A supplied global linear bound makes the given semilinear map continuous, with unchanged values. The proof uses additivity to bound differences; neither a nontrivially valued field nor exact scalar homogeneity is needed in this direction. It does not claim that every continuous map over arbitrary coefficients has such a bound. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=13) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/ContinuousLinearMap.lean#L55).

The structure is a semilinear equivalence preserving the given seminorm exactly. In the ordinary scalar case it is the standard isometric linear isomorphism. Bijectivity is separate data, which matters for nonseparated seminorms: norm preservation alone would not imply injectivity. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean#L432).

A semilinear isometric equivalence yields a continuous semilinear equivalence in both directions, with the same function. Its inverse is also an isometry, so inverse continuity needs no open-mapping theorem, completeness assumption or nontrivial scalar norm. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/math5020f11/breuningnotes.pdf#page=14) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/LinearIsometry.lean#L615).

The forward transport sends f to e₄₃ ∘ f ∘ e₁₂⁻¹; the inverse uses the two inverse compositions. This is the expected change of source and target for Hom spaces. The result is semilinear with scalar map σ₄₃ and claims no topology or operator-norm estimate on those Hom spaces. Compared with [the reference](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/linmultialg/dualmod.pdf#page=9) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Basic.lean#L557).

The class requires two distance bounds with constant one, separately in the scalar and vector variables. For distributive normed modules they follow from the contractive scalar inequality. The definition itself assumes only an action on pointed pseudometric spaces, so it records metric compatibility without adding module laws. Compared with [the reference](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Algebra.lean#L120).

This mixin records precisely the strong triangle inequality d(x,z)≤max(d(x,y),d(y,z)). Metric or pseudometric axioms come from separate structures. It therefore supports the standard ultrametric notion and its nonseparated version without silently asserting positivity, symmetry or separation from an arbitrary distance function. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Ultra/Basic.lean#L47).

An additive group with an ultrametric seminorm has a neighborhood basis at zero consisting of open additive subgroups. The proof takes positive-radius balls: the strong triangle inequality and negation invariance give subgroup closure. This is the topological nonarchimedean conclusion; it does not require local compactness or separation. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Ultra.lean#L195).

The bundle consists of a continuous map whose image has bounded diameter. For pseudometric targets this is the usual bounded-range condition and requires no distinguished origin. The existential bound is a property, not a chosen component of the function, so equal underlying functions represent the same object. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Basic.lean#L41).

Bounded continuous maps carry the uniform pseudometric supₓ d(f(x),g(x)). Boundedness makes this finite, and pointwise triangle inequalities give the function-space triangle inequality. The source defines it as an infimum of nonnegative upper bounds, which also assigns distance zero on an empty domain. Compared with [the reference](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/umtg.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Bounded/Basic.lean#L195).

Continuous functions on a compact domain inherit the uniform seminorm and pointwise additive group. The transfer through bounded continuous functions preserves the existing compact-open uniformity, rather than replacing it with pointwise convergence. No Hausdorff domain or separated coefficient norm is required. Compared with [the reference](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=538) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/ContinuousMap/Compact.lean#L172).

The topology is generated by subbasic sets of maps carrying a compact set K into an open set U. This is the standard compact-open topology, with finite intersections supplied by generateFrom. The definition requires neither local compactness nor Hausdorffness; those belong to later mapping-space theorems. Compared with [the reference](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=538) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/CompactOpen.lean#L51).

On a discrete space, compact subsets are precisely finite subsets, so the filter of complements of compact sets is the cofinite filter. This is the bridge that turns C₀ on a discrete index set into vanishing outside finite sets. It applies to arbitrary discrete spaces, not just natural numbers. Compared with [the reference](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/morris.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Compact.lean#L601).

Nonnegative powers of a base below one converge to zero in an Archimedean ordered semifield with its order topology. The zero base is handled after the initial term; for a positive base the proof inverts the divergent powers of its reciprocal. Completeness of the ordered field is unnecessary. Compared with [the reference](https://people.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/521.2017s/SequencesinR.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.lean#L189).

For positive x and y<1, some natural power of y is below x. No y≥0 premise is missing: if y≤0, n=1 already works; otherwise reciprocal powers grow beyond x⁻¹. The conclusion is existence of one small power, not convergence of the full power sequence. Compared with [the reference](https://people.math.wisc.edu/~angenent/521.2017s/SequencesinR.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Basic.lean#L249).

In a multiplicatively Archimedean linearly ordered commutative group, division by a unique integer power of a>1 moves b into (c,c·a]. The open-left, closed-right convention is correct: if b=c·aᵏ, the exponent is k−1. This is the multiplicative integer-part construction, without assuming real logarithms exist. Compared with [the reference](https://public.csusm.edu/aitken_html/m378_summer2019/Ch8SequencesLimits.pdf#page=10) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Basic.lean#L121).

Continuity follows from the projection-compatible evenly covered neighborhoods, although it is not a separate field of IsCoveringMap. At each e, the actual fiber over f(e) contains e, so the source can use a local trivialization there. Empty fibers elsewhere cause no exception. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, covering definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L336).

Around each point of E, fixing its discrete fiber coordinate selects an open sheet on which f is a homeomorphism onto an open base neighborhood. The conclusion is local homeomorphism, not global injectivity. No nonempty fiber away from the image or global surjectivity is required. Compared with [§1.3 pp.56 and 60, covering sheets and local homeomorphisms](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L339).

Images of open subsets of E are open in X because their intersections with covering sheets map homeomorphically to open sets. The source invokes the general local-homeomorphism result. Openness of a map does not mean surjectivity, which remains absent here. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, open-sheet definition; direct consequence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L342).

The predicate requires ambient evenly covered neighborhoods at every x∈s, using f’s full fiber. This correctly localizes the covering condition over s. It is stronger than merely saying the restricted map to the subspace s is a covering; it need not assert continuity of f away from f⁻¹(s). Compared with [§1.3 p.56, evenly covered neighborhoods; localized definition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L197).

Shrinking the set of base points from s to t⊆s preserves the ambient covering condition at those points. The direction of inclusion is correct: the same neighborhoods work for fewer points. No restriction or modification of f itself is performed. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, pointwise neighborhood condition](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L226).

Restricting the domain to f⁻¹(s) and the codomain to s gives a covering in their subspace topologies. Ambient sheets restrict to sheets over each relative neighborhood. The conclusion is valid for arbitrary s, including nonopen and empty sets. Compared with [§1.3 Exercise 1, p.79; local-on-s version checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L298).

A covering of f⁻¹(s)→s gives ambient evenly covered neighborhoods on s when both s and f⁻¹(s) are open in their ambient spaces. The two openness hypotheses convert relative open neighborhoods to ambient ones. Continuity of f globally is not assumed, so openness of its preimage cannot be silently dropped. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, neighborhood definition; converse to restriction checked with open subspaces](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L302).

An empty preimage of a whole neighborhood of x gives an evenly covered neighborhood with an empty sheet index. The source first chooses an open neighborhood inside U. An empty fiber at x alone would not suffice; the neighborhood hypothesis excludes nearby points entering the image. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, explicit allowance of an empty collection of sheets](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L134).

A bundle trivialization with discrete fiber I gives a product homeomorphism over its open base set. The condition x∈t.baseSet puts x inside that valid region, and the trivialization’s projection law ensures this is a trivialization of f. There is no claim about its arbitrary total values outside the source. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, evenly covered neighborhoods via discrete sheets](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L118).

The sheet index I can be replaced by the actual fiber over x, using the homeomorphism obtained by evaluating the local product at x. This preserves topology and projection compatibility. It works for empty fibers and asserts no canonical ordering or labeling of the sheets. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, sheets indexed by points of the fiber](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L114).

If the base lies in an open subspace s, an evenly covered relative neighborhood is also open in X after composing with subtype inclusion. Its preimage and product homeomorphism transfer unchanged up to the inclusion. Openness of s is the hypothesis that makes the ambient conclusion valid. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, ambient neighborhood condition; open-subspace consequence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L150).

A local product over U identifies i∈I with the inverse image of (x,i), giving a homeomorphism onto f⁻¹{x}. Conversely, the fiber coordinate of a point over x recovers i. The direction and subspace topology are correct; this construction chooses a valid local trivialization and is not a canonical sheet labeling. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, sheet/fiber correspondence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L48).

The conclusion is the local finite-fiber version of the closed-local-homeomorphism criterion. Hausdorffness of E separates each finite fiber into disjoint sheets; closedness excludes all other preimages over a smaller neighborhood. The inspected argument needs no connected or Hausdorff base, global continuity away from f⁻¹(s), or constant fiber count. Compared with [§1 lemma and §2 proof (2)⇒(3), pp.1–3; local generalization checked directly](https://web.math.utk.edu/~freire/teaching/m562s21/ProperCoverings.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L558).

A subset t of one fiber is discrete when every point has a local homeomorphism chart agreeing with f. In such a chart, injectivity makes that point the only member of t. The conclusion is discreteness in the subspace topology, not finiteness or closedness of t. Compared with [Proof, discrete-fiber argument before choosing disjoint sheets](https://www.matem.unam.mx/~omar/notes/propetale.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L497).

The hypotheses make Uᵢ∩f⁻¹(V) disjoint open sheets mapping homeomorphically onto V. The open-set iff supplies both directions of continuity, while injectivity, surjectivity and exhaustion give the product bijection. Nonempty ι and Nonempty(X→E) supply only total-function defaults outside the valid trivialization domain. Compared with [§1.3 p.56, disjoint-sheet characterization; construction checked directly](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Basic.lean#L438).

The orbit projection is a quotient covering for a free continuous action with compact-set proper discontinuity on a locally compact Hausdorff space. Local compactness supplies a compact neighborhood; only finitely many translates meet it, and separation plus freeness shrinks it to disjoint translates. Thus the input implies Hatcher’s covering-space-action condition. Compared with [§1.3 Exercise 23, p.81, and Proposition 1.40(a), p.72](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L283).

A quotient covering is equivalently a surjective covering with continuous group translations, a free action, and fibers exactly equal to orbits. For the reverse direction a single sheet cannot meet a nonidentity translate: projection equality and sheet injectivity give a fixed point, then freeness gives the identity. The separate surjectivity premise is necessary. Compared with [§1.3 p.72, condition (*) and Proposition 1.40; converse verified by sheet injectivity](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L336).

The subgroup consists of self-homeomorphisms h of E satisfying p∘h=p, with ordinary composition and inverse. This is the usual deck group for a covering, generalized coherently to any map p. Its algebraic closure uses only that equation, so no topology on X or continuity/covering hypothesis on p is needed. Compared with [§1.3 p.70, deck transformations as automorphisms over the base](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Deck.lean#L41).

Membership means the homeomorphism lies over the identity of the base: p(h(e))=p(e) for every e, written as equality of functions. No map of X is involved. The ambient type already supplies a continuous inverse, so a merely fiber-preserving endomorphism is not sufficient. Compared with [§1.3 p.70, automorphisms of a covering over its base](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Deck.lean#L51).

A quotient covering map is an open quotient map: its input supplies surjectivity, and the induced covering supplies continuity and openness. The output therefore retains all three properties. No normality classification, connectedness or separation assumption is added. Compared with [§1.3 p.72, quotient covering construction; open-sheet consequence](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean#L235).
